# Sublime and Beautiful Sunday This post is for #SublimeSunday is inspired by @c0ff33a and #BeautifulSunday is initiated by @ace108. I must admit now that the weather has been nicer, the most sublime and beautiful sight for me is catching a nice sunrise, and over the last week I have bene lucky to catch a few nice sunrises, and today will share some from an early morning walk at the port. Now Mother nature can put on such amazing displays but she keeps us on our toes as we never know what sunrise colors we may be fortunate to see. As I have mentioned I check the weather apps and look at what coulds they say are around and use that to pick where i may got for my morning walk. This day according to the weather apps I was not that hopeful of a nice sunrise, and decided to head to the port for a walk, I often go there as even if the sky is dull its a cool spot for photos, if I am thinking there is a god chance of nice sunrise colors I will oftenhead to a beach or pond as I do love sunrises caught over the water. but as it happenned that morning the apps or my interpretation of the clouds was wrong and I was lucky enough to catch a nice sunrise, and when not expecting it, then its even more sublime This shot was taken just behind where I parked my car that moning, the Halina M and the seastreak ferry building in the background

...as we wanted to see if the lake has filled up after recent storms.
![003.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23uQto8Bzbw6fAzxYf8EiLYEHGGkVabEkCQx4RJ3dgGP69iGfGbrWsuS9Dw9nMfKZi1Yx.jpg)

This is what it looked like during our last visit that I posted. But by now all of the flamingos were gone, as they migrate every winter here to the warmer countries up north on the African Continent. They will return during the late spring season next year, as they breed here. Then their youngsters grow up during our summer season to be strong enough for the migration trip the next winter.

We were happy to see that the lake is full again, and even more water will be added to sustain it now during our winter, as we are in a winter rainfall area. So, today you will see no flamingos, and none of the other migratory birds, as we had to search for any local birds that we may find. There was no water to be seen here during our last visit, as we could walk in the area where the water is now. 
Fortunally we found a few local birds that I will show you in here. 

![003.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EqquufEA6JDnEj4KPBsu2LsbEZTrEa12Vj64XNDGwWecZ1APF29byXRZAUGf2BiHfdZ.JPG)

![006.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/Eqqtpdf6ud86L9Jg9ihB6BB8bCawWzevXLYsjet7u7CDuKUnC6htf3H1uUBwnkGxySu.JPG)

No birds, not even one could be seen, and during summer there are thousands of birds all over here.
![008.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EqquSSsc6MGRiXRVveYSLYtfm7JREuQKSKfLrwdbJmZUAp24jdCH51X8AWoRcy7xKmk.JPG)

**But what was this?**

I saw the dive and knew that I was too close, so I stepped back to wait for the bird to emerge.
![009.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23uFYCuDUw3mUQD7hw7psfuz6GpL9aR8fXGdZB3jUZUgdKuJ1saCNZVxEKt9S1Ls12ubC.JPG)

Ah! It was a Red-knobbed Coot (Fulica cristata).
![010.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EoChDc29LBmX1rZ2F5TXHQaEYYp9BJQCwMeoER22ZpnzwJ3h9k8yKjVWS3Rire4maf3.JPG)

And now for a scoop, as look what I got below.
![021.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23z7DdDq5fpx1FKbve3odbQDChev1bPXgQGxS3rGcrLuQVwEEVDTHtUV9GB6yH9BVgtKE.JPG)

A lovely Swan couple, and it might be Black Swans (Cygnus atratus), but with the sun in my eyes I could not be certain as to the species.
![027.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EqL7GkvMWNUtv8NUNXamroYb4UeV1z8Sdk5BLL2dDbbQRAD5hkXyMJR11ifFWF3UWNu.JPG)

I know that they can be found in Australia, and someone might have brought them in, or they escaped from somewhere.
![025.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/Eos2DdA3m2DNrUjvyRDJJFtdi5ja5zvdqWnLfapRqMqNyfkbVGru9dH8fQoQKdtTifR.JPG)

Finally, I close with some attacking coots on a run in the lake.
![034.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/Eo4DyU55ZxAHfRFL3UW299yAxuKHhx1EuYU7u2xNmaBcfGwu39Ea9X8i9ii1ZpTcmCC.JPG)

We love our visits to this lake, as it has taught us so much about nature and the seasons. As much as the birds are dependent on the water, so we as human beings are also dependent on water. Only difference is that we cannot run on the water like the coots do :) Only joking, but yes, it is said that water is life, and here is evidence of it. The coots are tough little birds, and they fiercely protect their territories. If a strange coot appears, then they chase it by running after it on the water.

As far as the swans are concerned, we don't know them, but they are here, and so we will have to do some research to see what we can find. I should have done the research first before I did this post, but my excuse is that I am old and have a foggy brain, so don't ask me quickly what my name is :) In any case, I am sure that we will visit the lake again, and then when I do the post, I will have the information if I don't forget. 
Such is life. 

I hope you enjoyed the pictures and the story.

Photos by Zac Smith. All-Rights-Reserved.

Camera: Canon PowershotSX70HS Bridge camera. 

Thank you kindly for supporting this post.

I hope your weekend went well and wishing you a good week ahead. I am starting the week as I tend to do by sharing a few Monochrome Photos from recent walks. I was just thinking I am not sure I have ever discussed how I go about choosing photos to edit in mono, and for the most part I am not sure I have a deep thought process, just when I come to a photo and are ready to edit it, sometimes my mind clicks try this in MOnochrome. But thinking about it more this morning I said to myself, myself I said :) What is it about the photos that make smy brain tell me to try a Monochrome edit and this is what I came up with I fele a lot to do with it is if the photo has strong contrasts, intricate textures, and interesting and or compelling geometry thats what draws me to try monochrome editing. Stripping away color forces the viewer to focus on light, shadow, and form rather than being distracted by a messy over overwhelming color palette. And this first shot of the old Bridge out to Popes Island here in New Bedford is a good example of that

I recently became the owner of a new phone, so it was finally time to test its camera. As it happened yesterday I was at my nephew’s birthday party and they have a cat at home. I decided it would be the perfect opportunity to take a few photos. So, the star of today’s post is NORKA and her story.

Less than a year ago my nineteen-year-old nephew found a small, lost and undernourished kitten. I’m glad to have such a kind-hearted nephew. He took the kitten home, gave her food and water and cared for her. Norka stole the hearts of the whole family from the very first day. She was quickly accepted and it did not take long before the decision was made that she would stay with them permanently.

At first Norka was very frightened. She also displayed some unusual behaviors that were most likely caused by severe stress. However, she soon settled into her new home and those nervous habits gradually disappeared until they were completely gone.

Not long afterwards it turned out that Norka was deaf. Unfortunately, there is no way to cure her condition. The world as Norka experiences it is completely silent. She grew up in my sister’s home surrounded above all by love, care and affection.
At first, because she was deaf and never made any sounds, we thought she might not only be deaf but also mute. However, only quite recently she began producing her very first meows!

Now she is a friendly, happy cat who enjoys life!
I’m very happy that she was found in time and given a chance for a better life!

...and it's always a pleasure to see how the clouds fold over the peaks.
![002.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/48RPTRDZncrJBA2QKiHo6q1Pt8RfEohn6Ri8xhrhLiVbAhzYuAjo11YRFTo6TzjMtz.jpg)

Early morning shots and at the time I saw a band of cloud developing below the top of the mountains. I took some lovely landscapes of the band, as I had an idea what the views would look like later in the day, that I will show you in another post. So, we returned later in the afternoon, and we were happy to see what happened with the band of cloud. If you love mountains and landscapes as much as we do, then you will also like the views in here. 
But for now, let me just show you some of the morning shots.
Come and see.

![003.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/243WKW9tDwjpbRn41f3w2Q5AJBAjs8BPZ8eEjHpUNyfrL9tqRVRDWbQcQX7CJvk6wJfeK.JPG)

See that band of cloud above the ground, that is what I was talking about to get later in the day. 
![004.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/Eq9VCqfBUXLvXEaco1fBV2mzkkmdjXSjz4CT7LE5SoXLyQz73R1bpwgQbtxRH75ZoNi.JPG)

![005.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23uaEtE3VSmJFCLEE8g574oMkiCPyh8nLEu6L53A363Wdrxe2QnfShop86tiGu9jkyR1g.JPG)

The weather was holding up today, and although it was a cool day, as we are in winter here now, a weak winter sun was also shining on occasion. I have said in the previous post that the mountains can form their own clouds, and this was another of such occurrences. Beautiful to see how the clouds blanket the mountains. Thankfully a gentle wind was in action, and none of those hair-raising wind gusts.

On the other side of these mountains are some even higher mountains further inland, and can you believe that they are in the summer rainfall area. We have a Mediterranean climate here and the Atlantic Ocean is just a few kilometers away from us. So, the ocean also has a great effect in our weather patterns. Long white sandy beaches are packed with the visitors during the holiday periods.    

![013.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/Ep7uaRuRko5idhQ5TmMrs5yjvqecjFxFYyUgsmN2vNDz6dwpDrAixQFeGsWe3Hf9DNe.JPG)

![018.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/244KNmAHMoWqhH2u9pkR9kYWzLehMbe7khog7WLBph8gsQqyHn4RxmB9hJtDPLEkWz9D4.JPG)

![024.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23yTYxsWd4odhZM3NV4Dfq8sdrtoQ8tijk3yNHZtH9DfbK5LEYsDy6SE3y83SHXNbmKqh.JPG)

Finally, just a look at a single mountain towards the north of our mountain range. Lovely how that cloud rests on the left-hand peak. 
![020.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/245cRyNiUP3oyD2DoNqWqGkrt9w7h5NoXaD4yGtMcoRvEyDwG63FhSwL7K51suTWVAGrv.JPG)

As human beings we are so strange, as most of us are born with a want. I want this, I want that, and if I get it then I am not satisfied as I want more. Striving after our wants is a waste of time as we miss out on life and how it was supposed to be. Every new generation comes along with new things and most of it requires a faster response of adaption for the older generations. Just the other day I had to make calls through a switchboard operator and nowadays I can make a direct call on my wife's mobile phone. 

Unheard of in the 50's. I still have a turntable and a pack of records in a cupboard, and also an original old telephone. But those days, along with its strict ethics and morals, have now been binned, as anyone can do just what they like, whether it is legal or not. The media is filled with horror stories that fills one with dread, and things are really becoming a madhouse. That's one of the reasons that we like to visit the sanity of nature, as it is almost a doctor's treatment every time. 
Such is life. 

I hope you enjoyed the pictures and the story.

...and I open the post with a Camellia flower wearing a rainwater crown. 
![005.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/245HnoYUA3nXJFdhYdJn4oggSV59FMjBHq4F5x914BEY3wzaLFhHcFPtLKnUnRepR36qr.jpg)

Two parts in the post, as I also played a bit with the moon. The thing is that we expected no rain and yet for a few hours we had what we call fairy rain. Drops so small that one can barely feel them. Just a fine drizzle that wets everything very gently, and we were glad, especially after the damaging rainstorms and floods that we had to endure for the past days. I took some random shots during the day and thankfully the rain stopped. 

A dense mist had us drive very slowly with the car's lights on and we encountered no incidents on the roads. It seems the people have learnt how to drive in the wet, and one always has to be aware of some people's love to ignore the red traffic lights. Red means stop and wait for the green, but we have many chancers that simply drive through the red lights. Then another irritant is also those with the "loud" cars, the ones that try to sound like a rocket and the noise scares even the rain away.

Just to show you what the view looked like early morning. 
![001.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23ywoF66YwqzfFoKSQAJ5TwMrYKHsxYi3KXvgLZVssSPZscpvPdW7rNJBQLgu3wLgnt73.JPG)

In the second part of the post, I will show you some moon shots, as the sun seemed to light it up. The month of May has two full moons, and I missed the first one as the skies were covered in cloud, and so I will get a second chance to get the full moon on the 31st of May. I just hope that the clouds will read this post and give me a chance to get the full moon :)   

![100.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/23u5tEBNe21WJAmA6McAaZY9uoDvemsHbBNSaBfJRzHPnqRGiboFU9ig3TGNwxo5wj3Ln.JPG)

This photo below is where I at first became aware of the moon as the cloud opened up. 
![072.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EopmaCtXM1VJ5iFAT7qG6DjAvwzYnPp242sZcMQg3NA9CnuEZMUfDfdXPY7gjhqPAGX.JPG)

But it wasn't going to be for long, and I only had a chance to get a few shots.
![103.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/EoJyyUsHDUBzeFK1D6JiwUmnc3rv7xwuKzgnkv3mJHNnZtWzvC9AzjhwZQbvRTgvepH.JPG)

Finally, the cloud became jealous, and it closed the moon again, but by then I had enough shots.
![105.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/papilloncharity/Ep7sdceTqW9tysNK4YVdzKTh7sbiEsnYKWxugD3qLFvNJmZ8w3ZEBFsK1w7dDwh71mF.JPG)

I like to play in the sky as I am a being that belongs in the sky, at least it feels like that to me. Nary a day goes by that I do not have my eyes on the sky. Yes, I know that there are also abundant views for a photographer on the land, and I do try to combine the elements whenever I am out taking photos. Variety is the name of the game as it prevents one's offerings from becoming stale.

Nature, of course, has its own treasures for those of us that take a more concentrated look at things, and it holds a trove of surprises. One can learn nature's laws just via the medium of photography as everything in nature has a role in the eco-systems. Nothing goes to waste and the wetlands even filter the river water that flows into it. Just a pity that so many don't understand this as littering just continues to take place. 
Such is life. 

I hope you enjoyed the pictures and the story.

Until next time, cheers!

result.body: My city might just be a reflection of what is happening in much of the world. A place where the past still remains standing while the present continues trying to draw the future, little by little. It is strange to think about that, because many of the things that today seem modern or even like something new will, a few years from now, also be seen as part of a time left behind. It sounds like something too obvious to say, but when we stop to truly observe, we realize how everything happens silently. We are so used to this mixture before our eyes that we almost never notice that, one day, what we call the present today will also become just a memory. When I walk through the city, this mixture between past and present becomes very evident. The city never stops growing. Spaces keep getting smaller, especially downtown, where it feels like every available piece has already been occupied. And then the most common solution appears: growing upward. Floor upon floor, bigger and bigger buildings trying to find space where there is almost no space left at all. But the most curious thing is how this transformation happens without us fully noticing it. Little by little, everything starts blending together. Modern, mirrored, gleaming constructions begin sharing the landscape with old buildings that still carry marks of another era. And many times, all it takes is looking at the reflection on a glass surface to notice the contrast: the new reflecting the old, as if two different versions of the city were coexisting at the same time. And aren’t they? I particularly like that. There is something interesting about realizing how patterns change over the years. Ways of building, styles, and details that once seemed natural slowly disappear, giving place to new ideas, new aesthetics, and new needs. The city changes, but it still keeps fragments of what it once was. Maybe that is why these Sunday walks always leave me feeling a bit reflective. Walking among these concrete giants ends up being, in a certain way, like walking between different eras. Many times we pass through these places in a hurry without realizing that there is history hidden in every old facade or in every modern building that continues to rise. In the end, I think it is beautiful to notice that. Looking at the past still standing before us while the future continues being built right there, before our eyes. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXAvoao5G7Pgn6zBLdHPLBnKKy1VTjk34wZNusECxc5ez/image.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXr5nYZHrkpqik3hm1TGcNrCkkMVwwaPKmZEofmgLryA6/image.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPd4C2ghFkcA3p5nizauZn7kukMzpasPNHoCGgq9gXxhq/image.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfXYAaxJJ3wdcwGzhxMAhDyZW18SjeGViS1vJrrJKZ7GR/image.png) Minha cidade talvez seja apenas um reflexo do que está acontecendo em boa parte do mundo. Um lugar onde o passado ainda permanece de pé enquanto o presente continua tentando desenhar o futuro, pouco a pouco. É estranho pensar nisso, porque muitas das coisas que hoje parecem modernas ou até novidade, daqui alguns anos também serão vistas como parte de um tempo que ficou para trás. Parece algo óbvio de se dizer, mas, quando paramos para observar de verdade, percebemos como tudo acontece de forma silenciosa. Estamos tão acostumados com essa mistura diante dos nossos olhos que quase nunca percebemos que, um dia, aquilo que hoje chamamos de presente será apenas lembrança também. Quando caminho pela cidade, essa mistura entre passado e presente fica muito evidente. A cidade não para de crescer. Os espaços vão diminuindo, principalmente no centro, onde parece que cada pedaço disponível já foi ocupado. E então surge a solução mais comum: crescer para cima. Andares sobre andares, prédios cada vez maiores tentando encontrar espaço onde já quase não existe mais espaço algum. Mas o mais curioso é como essa transformação acontece sem que a gente perceba completamente. Aos poucos, tudo vai se misturando. Construções modernas, espelhadas e reluzentes, passam a dividir cenário com prédios antigos que ainda carregam marcas de outra época. E, muitas vezes, basta olhar o reflexo de um vidro para enxergar o contraste: o novo refletindo o velho, como se duas versões diferentes da cidade coexistissem ao mesmo tempo. E não existem? Eu particularmente gosto disso. Existe algo interessante em perceber como os padrões mudam com o passar dos anos. Formas de construir, estilos, detalhes que antes pareciam naturais vão desaparecendo devagar, dando lugar a novas ideias, novas estéticas e novas necessidades. A cidade muda, mas ainda guarda fragmentos do que já foi um dia. Talvez seja por isso que esses passeios de domingo sempre me deixam um pouco reflexivo. Caminhar entre esses gigantes de concreto acaba sendo, de certa forma, caminhar entre diferentes épocas. Muitas vezes passamos apressados por esses lugares sem perceber que existe história escondida em cada fachada antiga ou em cada prédio moderno que continua surgindo. No fim, acho bonito perceber isso. Olhar para o passado ainda presente diante de nós, enquanto o futuro continua sendo construído bem ali, diante dos nossos olhos.

>Some art exhibitions surprise me, others amaze me; in others, I find myself questioning things or reflecting, but in most I simply enjoy each piece and what the artist conveys. --- ![Image_1779561497591.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23wX5UvaAdeiJ3MhUwjuVz5Y2L1fyMkMmmMe9Hoz8i3K7FfQneVKhBuwQ4F4tbvCeUGsR.jpg) --- Some time ago, I was able to visit one of the wonderful temporary exhibitions held every so often at the city’s Picasso Museum. These exhibitions aren’t confined to a small room; instead, the space has a labyrinthine structure, where a large area is divided into smaller sections depending on the theme. The walls are always changing colour, depending on the artist and how they wish to highlight the works, and the truth is that the museum does an extraordinary job. Until that day, I was unaware of the great work of the surrealist artist Óscar Domínguez, who is on a par with Miró, Picasso, Dalí and many others of his era, a difficult time, when many had to live in France or travel there for their art to be recognised. --- ![20251005_182714.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23wgaTfFWE7zCt1ccp6orwYgSyuBLL721SjFwmGrR9pGJKXw7qKoGFMYdNvRaB2FaWexd.jpg) --- ![20251005_183056.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/242466UsWTMk5YudniiYvv6cvqcy3Bxhx6h7ji9hKWy1VWJPMCyM2Sg2wfpioYsKTFmr8.jpg) “I Am Right, Surrealist Effect. “Can Opener”, 1936, oil on canvas. --- ![20251005_183302.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/24243ugnrMVSWzVo21tEndf5Mzd3oryy1LfccinAr5WqRPJYpxZAGmDNu2VuGVvyNuoca.jpg) “Spring”, 1939, oil on canvas. --- ![20251005_183319.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23ydByi55HcXpLcVdz4YLA5tahzhoqFV92DdURtJVSpwyPF2Xq91x3qtdUjUHe4jcQ1PX.jpg) “Surrealist Figures”, 1937, oil on canvas. --- ![20251005_183447.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23xAnjNM4ndzTs23xdMsKqjuxGfQGBAzaNudWQMiDMq45yz8iHDc1gf1rSyTD2E4gtKxq.jpg) “Apparition over the Sea”, 1939, oil on canvas. --- I often see surrealist art, even if it isn’t real, as a way of expressing oneself in a coded form, and that, on the other side, there will eventually be someone who sees something in a painting that resonates with them personally. I like to think that, because every artist has the canvas before them like a blank sheet of paper through which they can say many things, both personal and things they know, and perhaps it is the only way to express what they believe, see or feel. That is why I think art is wonderful and every artist has their own special way of doing things. This artist’s work is very good; I enjoyed standing there looking at each painting and observing both the colours he had used and his way of interpreting moments in life, sensations or experiences. --- ![20251005_183535.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23wCJADMzSKBj2YvTAeWR7cMJ7erDGshHzB52BiZeXqaqmbCN9j1ApkF52Xghd23KNw8U.jpg) “Delfos”, 1957, oil on canvas. --- ![20251005_183547.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/242hcxtVbaCN6wkaMmFhekoACz4H99MCRyrCe9AA8tx1mzCkJHabUR4NaFNwU4dLTf1Zr.jpg) “Los sifones”, 1938, oil on canvas. --- ![20251005_183606.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23xyhgBVfNsCSNiGKKrrJJJtSDmTxCHniT1KbhBBXhwYS1ycVHb41zgsgH68hsa5JWjU8.jpg) “The Road Roller and the Rose”, 1957, oil on canvas. --- ![20251005_183835.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23xpPNtqvx2z4qN3EQ7i3BJV8ejf9js5d5MBchntFcUCvsa3bT8Tz21aD2dncCcsZqmJg.jpg) “Lithochronic Figures”, 1939, oil on canvas. --- It is a form of surrealism brimming with magic, as if we were stepping through a door into a world that leads to unexpected places, where we can see strange shapes, figures and creatures. And there will always be one painting that we like more than another. In my case, I was drawn more to those with brighter, cheerful colours, rather than the dark or gloomy paintings, although of course they all have something worth seeing. On the other hand, as I looked at the paintings, another thing I particularly liked was that they all have a great sense of movement, as if what the artist wanted to express and everything he painted were moving to the beat of an invisible music, music with a special vibration that brought colour to some parts of the painting, light to others, and finally various shadows. Many of the works are among my favourites, such as ‘Apparition over the Sea’, ‘Surrealist Figures’, ‘The Piano’ and ‘I Am Right’. It’s hard to choose just one. If you have a favourite, I’d love to hear about it in the comments. --- ![20251005_183811.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23u6FdFjXYPt8mhUde34gjtKBwARTi2GYLs91vLbjWUYhRCJ9X1S9GqGXZdEJpT8jVmfD.jpg) “House”, Jacques Hérold, 1959, oil on canvas. --- ![20251005_183859.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23wMkuh8sSgkbDpjDvwXjqAMpZqB44xhenRCngRWkjvkgsKzGpFKVuSpbt8utisnsSaGr.jpg) “Psychological Morphology”, Roberto Mata, 1938, oil on canvas. ---
![20251005_183934.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/EqWnndQfJfR4WXkpwMpTqPE1LgRdbGk4DKdJaqTMRnWuQN6s5hjUFDAApESojaTm7Nm.jpg)
“Morgane”, Kurt Seligmann, 1951, oil on canvas. --- Three works by other artists accompanied this art exhibition; all three were equally spectacular. Of these three, the last one is my favourite. --- ![20251005_184152.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/avdesing/23vsQfLozGTtSAUPBFrsPD8GNZL1S96vxEjbrC5odfFFhJMxMGBoLMUcUryCbB3oJZ8Ds.jpg) --- In one of the corners of a very dark room, I think I found confirmation of what I said earlier: a grand piano stood there to accompany a spectacular art exhibition. The atmosphere was perfect; the lighting and the harmony of the rooms allowed me to fully appreciate the work of this great artist. Thank you very much for joining me today; I wish you all a very happy Sunday. See you soon. It is almost the end of May, and the spring vibes are fading in Beijing as temperatures rise faster than at the start of spring in April.  The afternoon is getting longer as the days grow longer, and the days are now brighter than in the springtime. As a result, daytime temperatures are also crossing the 25-degree mark, making the days like summer days. These photos I have taken in the park area in Beijing city during early spring when it was at its fullest. I found these scenic, iconic views of the city park while I was enjoying a walk in nature.

The location of the park is in the city area, so I found a lot of visitors in the park area, as you can see in these photos. As Beijing is so large, there are so many parks in the city, and I always love to explore scenic spots like the Summer Palace, Xiangshan Park, and Fragrant Hills Park, which are so beautiful and attractive to visit. 

I hope you enjoy my photos of the beautiful natural beauty of the Beijing city park. It is a great time to enjoy some outdoor activity like walking in this amazing area with warmer weather after the freezing cold of the winter season in Beijing. If you have any questions, let me know in the comments, and I will do my best to answer them.

Thanks a lot for your time and attention. I will catch up with you at the next one.

Wishing you a good day!

>I took all the photos, and these are my own property.

Hello fellow photography enthusiasts of this beautiful community! It's been a while since I've shared anything new. I've decided to revisit the forgotten piers of my city, so I visited the Junco Sur neighborhood, a peripheral area filled with buildings constructed mainly during the final years of the Soviet era. This neighborhood was founded in April 1986, and a pier was built near a beach there so that workers constructing the nuclear power plant could travel to the city of the same name, located on the other side of Jagua Bay. To reach the beach and the pier, which were once very popular, there was a road that is now a neglected and dilapidated track.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZBfLkVtc12bwGsLyKkEX98TeB9EexdrjN5mpu4qwu8gd/20260522_175114.jpg)

But it is in these forgotten spaces where beauty is often found.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaVxX4wYmZFEJUsZjWzyzdAvPEhunnqDneCgjabTsAESh/20260522_173311.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdqdS6QM1HHj5Zpi7Mn6xWHYmXxrrzTGSMTjZC86DU73S/20260522_173341.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma2kZuUD5hU7SeNbuL31f9gfwTB8YpT9L45EeiRW5Jh6V/20260522_173349.jpg)

Nature, as always, begins to reclaim the space that was taken from it, especially when humans cover up spaces through neglect. However, in this solitude and oblivion, I have been able to find the most sublime art for my phone's lens.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWREB2ZZrpfwRTapHKRGqmXXqVPZx1tWgvkwjofHZ5kCL/20260522_173416.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVsNuprsSc5azF4PnM86kiJj5keoEFekPAtXtE97uMXt6/20260522_173429.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUiYYNqwPqhzUdbLkLPP4y6AAQ7fDjhZBcR6dVZiBLq7D/20260522_173507.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSWvAemtpeCNfsULebgtSHN9XPtSAVkidgyS15r63fK1X/20260522_173541.jpg)

When I started taking pictures of the pier, I noticed that some people still come to this place to enjoy its tranquility and engage in fishing activities, an activity as old as humankind itself.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcBsJ5ydNz2mDrANfGHorxjUqQC7Efnr6RyVNw3thVmpi/20260522_173602.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTGrZLCCASuJKn4A7iP8tQsznkMgYKLFsRtL8XipdFGse/20260522_173609.jpg)

As happens in places where no maintenance is carried out, rust has taken over and corroded the foundations.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma7K5r1XB9yGg72t1CqCHB7UrLYoi5T8isRz8PGJtjDYp/20260522_173622.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbQWWJeftTysQzrJw6yV64NBbpUB5v6CaumZVnWtvykiy/20260522_173639.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbXJK3WQWG8jiRJbg3APd6Gn9Z2agSj7NcHNCUBNrw3dB/20260522_173647.jpg)

I remember my mother bringing me to this beach when we visited one of my aunts who still lives in this neighborhood. We often took different boats to the Nuclear City or another one dedicated to outdoor activities, belonging to a now-defunct recreational association known as SEPMI.

This rusty piece reminds me of the mooring knots that helped boats dock.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZm6JpxQFBQ1GUYUDGwENn7aZeiLFzgS3eMuomW75txEK/20260522_173833.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmV8i2DdQmwEKgK9QBbVWKNRmaTPspLjwW8NbS4JEcLsPC/20260522_173847.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWUT746M4KgYV2JKjQRonNBxmg7T4Mu7WJ42rK1TnEDRC/20260522_173907.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdvZDRfcapgy36NJFTbMFxaDTkhi1REtdxVVonnpmnFYf/20260522_173919.jpg)

There were also light towers that have since disappeared; this image looks like it's from another planet, like mountains in a cursed desert.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSFyFLWPK48j7EfDzcPTRzp1HVUsWMLd7Z3MfQf7YhFJS/20260522_174126.jpg)

Then there's the sea, that beautiful space that sometimes makes us feel so small, so insignificant in the face of such power and beauty. I hope one day I can take underwater photos and revel in the beauty of the vastness of the waters.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfDThxs3gMbLwoMUpZA3c1FoHVQceeaZvhVSY47Zu5KK9/20260522_174144.jpg)

I couldn't resist taking these photos, a must-have on a pier and in a city that lives on the sea. Fishing lines, or fishing in the most traditional Cuban way, without rods, with all the tranquility in the world to wait for the right fish, or the one destined to catch.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTKJfZHFKxi5LCuDdrxi9orDHNQs7jkjS4Xa5afx2VdDb/20260522_174255.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNzsutnqdE4cscK1za5cnncbJ167hUkhmdAT7St1NG4BW/20260522_174315.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVzZf3cnDXdPfU2EigXAMJBhRWhHZU7exoitLHuVah61G/20260522_174440.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZsoUpvKaghEAzggRokEhivi3dhWyz1YQickqg5wi3swZ/20260522_174640.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXAGVCJFsCp4EEptwu65dN5xKHLwe7wbjLG6y5SoFVWhS/20260522_174901.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbGgqhumt26MQHkjtKzuYTeprZvoDBQUyqminGTcg8WeG/20260522_174911.jpg)
As I was about to leave, a dog and its owner were enjoying the space. I hope you liked these photos.

Hola amigos amantes de la fotografía de esta hermosa comunidad, hace un tiempo que no mostraba nada nuevo. he decidido retomar los muelles olvidados de mi ciudad, por eso visite el barrio de Junco sur, un barrio periférico lleno de edificios construidos en la última etapa la era soviética principalmente. Es un barrio que se fundó en abril de 1986 y en el se construyó un muelle cerca de una playa, para que los trabajadores que trabajaban en la construcción de la central electro-nuclear viajaran hasta la ciudad de mismo nombre que esta al otro lado de la Bahía de Jagua. 
Para llegar a la playa y el muelle que eran muy visitados, existía una carretera que actualmente es un camino olvidado y en mal estado.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZBfLkVtc12bwGsLyKkEX98TeB9EexdrjN5mpu4qwu8gd/20260522_175114.jpg)

Pero es en estos espacios olvidados donde muchas veces se encuentra la belleza.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmaVxX4wYmZFEJUsZjWzyzdAvPEhunnqDneCgjabTsAESh/20260522_173311.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdqdS6QM1HHj5Zpi7Mn6xWHYmXxrrzTGSMTjZC86DU73S/20260522_173341.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma2kZuUD5hU7SeNbuL31f9gfwTB8YpT9L45EeiRW5Jh6V/20260522_173349.jpg)

La naturaleza como siempre comienza a cobrar el espacio que le fue tomada, más cuando el ser humano cubre los espacios con el desuso. sin embargo en esta soledad y olvido he podido encontrar el arte más sublime para el lente de mi teléfono.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWREB2ZZrpfwRTapHKRGqmXXqVPZx1tWgvkwjofHZ5kCL/20260522_173416.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVsNuprsSc5azF4PnM86kiJj5keoEFekPAtXtE97uMXt6/20260522_173429.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUiYYNqwPqhzUdbLkLPP4y6AAQ7fDjhZBcR6dVZiBLq7D/20260522_173507.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSWvAemtpeCNfsULebgtSHN9XPtSAVkidgyS15r63fK1X/20260522_173541.jpg)

Cuando comencé a tomar las fotos del muelle, percibí que algunas personas aún viene a este lugar para disfrutar de su tranquilidad y realizar actividades de pesca, una acción tan antigua como el propio ser humano.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcBsJ5ydNz2mDrANfGHorxjUqQC7Efnr6RyVNw3thVmpi/20260522_173602.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTGrZLCCASuJKn4A7iP8tQsznkMgYKLFsRtL8XipdFGse/20260522_173609.jpg)

Como ocurre en los lugares en los que no se realiza mantenimiento el oxido ha compensado a corroer los cimientos.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma7K5r1XB9yGg72t1CqCHB7UrLYoi5T8isRz8PGJtjDYp/20260522_173622.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbQWWJeftTysQzrJw6yV64NBbpUB5v6CaumZVnWtvykiy/20260522_173639.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbXJK3WQWG8jiRJbg3APd6Gn9Z2agSj7NcHNCUBNrw3dB/20260522_173647.jpg)

Recuerdo que mi madre me traía a esta playa cuando veníamos de visita a casa de una de mis tías que aún vive en esta barriada. Incluso muchas veces tomamos diferentes barcos hacia la Ciudad Nuclear u otro que estaba dedicado a las actividades al aire libre y que pertenecía a una asociación de esparcimiento que ya no existe y que era conocida con el nombre de SEPMI.
Esta pieza oxidada me recuerda los nudos de amarre que ayudaban a los barcos a atracar.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZm6JpxQFBQ1GUYUDGwENn7aZeiLFzgS3eMuomW75txEK/20260522_173833.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmV8i2DdQmwEKgK9QBbVWKNRmaTPspLjwW8NbS4JEcLsPC/20260522_173847.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWUT746M4KgYV2JKjQRonNBxmg7T4Mu7WJ42rK1TnEDRC/20260522_173907.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdvZDRfcapgy36NJFTbMFxaDTkhi1REtdxVVonnpmnFYf/20260522_173919.jpg)

También existían torres de luz que ya desaparecieron, esta imagen parece salida de otro planeta, como si fueran montañas en un desierto maldito.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSFyFLWPK48j7EfDzcPTRzp1HVUsWMLd7Z3MfQf7YhFJS/20260522_174126.jpg)
 Luego el mar, ese hermoso espacio que a veces nos hace sentir tan pequeño, tan esmirriado ante tanto poder y belleza. Espero algún día poder tomar fotos submarinas y deleitarme con la belleza de la inmensidad de las aguas.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfDThxs3gMbLwoMUpZA3c1FoHVQceeaZvhVSY47Zu5KK9/20260522_174144.jpg)

No pude dejar de tomar estas fotos que nunca pueden faltar en un muelle y en una ciudad que vive dentro del mar. Los hilos de pesca, o la pesca a la usanza más tradicional en Cuba, sin varas de pesca y con toda la tranquilidad del mundo para esperar a que llegue el pez adecuado o el destinado.
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmTKJfZHFKxi5LCuDdrxi9orDHNQs7jkjS4Xa5afx2VdDb/20260522_174255.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNzsutnqdE4cscK1za5cnncbJ167hUkhmdAT7St1NG4BW/20260522_174315.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYT1TzrNA3E7JLHqP2Dk2DiXsG6e5MuAsK25soXaiHUv3/20260522_174556.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZsoUpvKaghEAzggRokEhivi3dhWyz1YQickqg5wi3swZ/20260522_174640.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXAGVCJFsCp4EEptwu65dN5xKHLwe7wbjLG6y5SoFVWhS/20260522_174901.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbGgqhumt26MQHkjtKzuYTeprZvoDBQUyqminGTcg8WeG/20260522_174911.jpg)

### Spring on the Mountain
#

People who live up in the mountains need a little more patience for the feeling of spring to arrive. In town, I see some flowers blooming earlier than they do here in the mountains, even though it’s only a 10–15-minute drive away. I finally feel the full energy of spring on my property and throughout the neighbourhood.

![IMG_5231.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmP626WxfHyw5V6ooR95GHfCrCzwBGF6XJfDSzxyE1Q6CZ/IMG_5231.jpeg)

The spring air is very fresh and gentle, birds are actively singing, flowers are blooming happily, and the sky is beautifully blue and clear. On the other hand, many different kinds of bugs appear, such as black flies, no-see-ums, worms, bees, wasps, horse flies, and even ticks. The black flies, no-see-ums, and horse flies are especially bad because they bite us a lot. They are quite aggressive. I have severe allergies, and they seem to come to me constantly. Once they bite me, my body reacts strongly. Ticks are also scary for both humans and dogs. Luckily, my dog is white, so I can find them easily. I can avoid the flies once the spring breeze starts. They disappear quickly after that.

![IMG_5236.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmU8Fmskk3cXKyT8eMDTYuPbMRd3jFo5NKUXbkzVXNKuEm/IMG_5236.jpeg)

Well, from now on, I would like to talk about the beautiful side of spring in the mountains. Almost all of the trees have started smiling, and they have become so chatty. I can hear them around my property as well. I noticed that there are many young pine trees, birch trees, trembling aspens, and more. The young trees look so pretty and healthy. Unfortunately, I lost a few of our trees during storms over the past few years. My husband cut up those fallen trees this spring. They will become our firewood for the coming winter.

![IMG_5233.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSLxE1AK7yMV4axLwEh97Lcx9i8yiiEcevGxAW1BgxVRu/IMG_5233.jpeg)

The apple trees have started blooming beautifully. Apple blossoms are so lovely. The Apple Blossom Festival is happening this week. This 92-year-old historical festival is a very popular event for local people as well as tourists.

![IMG_5229.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSCfoXeCKFFVGhrsruAyc5bsADQGS2KiLNyN4aBDiQYET/IMG_5229.jpeg)

This bird cherry tree is such a beautiful symbol on my property. Usually, it starts blooming in the middle of May. Now, it looks so gorgeous and graceful. This year, a bird family is living in it. They sing every day, especially in the morning and during the daytime. I think my husband trimming the broken branches earlier this spring helped the flowers become especially healthy.

![IMG_5228.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZxmSB4kNRcB6aNJzEsnJHUc6uigpAeQTWjSi8Pkk4yqW/IMG_5228.jpeg)

Also, woodpeckers are very active on my property this year. My dog has become friends with one of them. The young, handsome woodpecker usually starts pecking at our fence very early in the morning. When my dog wakes up, he goes outside with me to see the woodpecker. Sometimes, I can hear them very early in the morning from my bedroom. The pecking sound feels like a rhythmic clock or something similar. It’s not as noisy as you might imagine.

![IMG_5230.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeTE89kF2gdHSUW2inxwy3yc2tD6XdiEvK9qNFrzzd9Dc/IMG_5230.jpeg)

Almost all of the dandelions are finishing blooming and turning into fluffy seed heads. I love dandelion fluff very much. My dog really likes visiting the big field near my house. However, when manure is spread on the field, we can’t visit it. Luckily, this year the farmer is letting the land rest, so we can visit it sometimes. Still, we have to be careful about ticks once the grass grows tall.

![IMG_5232.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTWpFP58WiqtRzoFtw6trYsYvSqdtRCMRivVjjPrzWdk8/IMG_5232.jpeg)

I hope you enjoy my mountain spring photos. Probably, most of your spring flowers and plants have already finished blooming.

![IMG_5226.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbUx7fG8GRTw5cqEkgcSVu3UQjXpPX6DnseZbPQ1zAPbR/IMG_5226.jpeg)

![IMG_5227.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRxerYzADLvGRqHJLDpNtkJnp1Jed9Pjx3FYKRvHssTof/IMG_5227.jpeg)

Japanese 日本語

![IMG_5235.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcvDhmrhJby87R4g5126pRmzQwTBQ8bwss1LQWutDdgEZ/IMG_5235.jpeg)
### 山の春
#

山に住んでいる人たちは、春らしい空気を感じるまでに、通常よりも少しだけ長めの忍耐が必要です。町では、ここよりも早く花が咲いているのを見かけます。たった１０〜１５分ほど車で走っただけで、山とは季節の進み方が違います。ようやく私の家の敷地や近所全体にも、本格的な春の息吹を感じられるようになりました。

![IMG_5231.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmP626WxfHyw5V6ooR95GHfCrCzwBGF6XJfDSzxyE1Q6CZ/IMG_5231.jpeg)

春の空気はとても新鮮でやわらかく、鳥たちは元気にさえずり、花々は嬉しそうに咲き、空は青く澄み渡っています。その一方で、ブラックフライ、ヌカカ、小さな虫、蜂、スズメバチ、アブ、さらにはダニまで、さまざまな虫たちも出現しはじめます。特にブラックフライやヌカカ、アブはとても厄介で、かなり刺されます。本当に攻撃的なので困ります。かなりひどいアレルギーがあるからか、なぜか虫たちがしつこく寄ってきます。一度刺されると、体が強く反応してしまいます。ダニも、人間にも犬にも怖い存在です。でも幸い、私の犬は白いので、ダニを見つけやすいです。春の強い風が吹き始めると、ハエたちは少し避けやすくなり、しばらくの間どこかに消えてくれます。

![IMG_5236.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmU8Fmskk3cXKyT8eMDTYuPbMRd3jFo5NKUXbkzVXNKuEm/IMG_5236.jpeg)

さて、ここからは山の春の美しい部分についてお話ししたいと思います。ほとんどの木々が笑顔になってきたように見え、とてもおしゃべりな感じになりました。私の敷地の中でも、その声が聞こえてくるようです。あっという間に若い松の木、白樺、ポプラなどがたくさん育っていることにも気づきました。若い木々はとても美しく、健康そうです。残念ながら、ここ数年の嵐で何本かの木がダメになってしまいました。今年の春、主人がその倒れた木々を切ってくれました。それらは次の冬の薪になります。

![IMG_5233.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSLxE1AK7yMV4axLwEh97Lcx9i8yiiEcevGxAW1BgxVRu/IMG_5233.jpeg)

リンゴの木の花も美しく咲き始めました。りんごの花は本当にきれいです。今週はアップルブロッサム・フェスティバルが開催されています。この９２年続く歴史あるお祭りは、地元の人々だけでなく観光客にもとても人気があります。

![IMG_5229.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSCfoXeCKFFVGhrsruAyc5bsADQGS2KiLNyN4aBDiQYET/IMG_5229.jpeg)

このバードチェリーの木は、私の敷地の中で特別な象徴のような存在です。いつも５月半ば頃に満開になりますが、ちょうど今は本当に優雅で美しく見えます。今年は鳥の家族がこの木に住んでいます。毎日、特に朝から昼間にかけて、その鳥たちの声が聞こえてきます。今年の早春に主人が折れた枝を剪定してくれたので、そのおかげで花がとても元気に咲いているのだと思います。

![IMG_5228.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZxmSB4kNRcB6aNJzEsnJHUc6uigpAeQTWjSi8Pkk4yqW/IMG_5228.jpeg)

また、今年はキツツキたちもとても活発です。私の犬は、そのうちの一羽と仲良くなりました。その若くてハンサムなキツツキは、朝早くから私たちのフェンスをコツコツ叩き始めます。私の犬は起きると、私と一緒に外へ出て、そのキツツキを見に行きます。時には寝室から、その音がかなり早朝から聞こえてくることもあります。木を叩く音は、まるでリズミカルな時計のようです。想像するほど騒がしい音ではありません。

![IMG_5230.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeTE89kF2gdHSUW2inxwy3yc2tD6XdiEvK9qNFrzzd9Dc/IMG_5230.jpeg)

ほとんどのタンポポは咲き終わり、綿毛になり始めています。私はタンポポの綿毛がとても好きです。私の犬は、家の近くにある大きな野原へ行くのが大好きです。でも、そこに肥料がまかれると、しばらくの間は行くことができません。今年は農家の方がその土地を休ませるようなので、ときどき訪れることができそうです。ただ、草が伸びてくるとダニには気をつけなければいけません。

![IMG_5232.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTWpFP58WiqtRzoFtw6trYsYvSqdtRCMRivVjjPrzWdk8/IMG_5232.jpeg)

私の山の春の写真を楽しんでもらえたら嬉しいです。きっと、皆さんの地域では、春の花や植物はもう終わりかけている頃かもしれません。

![IMG_5226.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbUx7fG8GRTw5cqEkgcSVu3UQjXpPX6DnseZbPQ1zAPbR/IMG_5226.jpeg)

![IMG_5227.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRxerYzADLvGRqHJLDpNtkJnp1Jed9Pjx3FYKRvHssTof/IMG_5227.jpeg)

Thank you for reading!

##### Hi everyone :)

Take a good look at the visual mess I encountered in this session.
I don't dislike it, but I found it a bit confusing, especially when I looked at the set of photos and realized that everything looked kind of similar, dark, and abstract.

But when we look more closely, focusing on each of the results, the scenario transforms and we discover those always curious and mysterious details.

---

##### Session Purpose

In these sessions of macro photography, or objective, in order to spend a good amount of time reflecting on oneself, and go as long as possible in no detail, within the limits of the technique that is to be used, of course, sometimes it is difficult to obtain the result that is initially intended, it is better to always make the effort. What interests me is to look carefully, really stop in front of the chosen object and record everything that it reveals, opting for different angles and perspectives, recording the textures, the small irregularities, different contrasts and those small marks that normally go unnoticed. There is also a very visual side to this process, because I don't just want to document, I want to build interesting visual compositions. When I publish this work on my blog, I intend to share this experience of close observation and show the discreet beauty and complexity that exists, many times in the most banal objects, others not so much.

<center><sub>F-stop: F/5 | Exposure time: 1/200 sec. | ISO speed: ISO 400</sub></center>

---

There are not several ways to shoot macro photography, but among the possible ways, this is, for me, one of the most simple and mainly the most accessible and very effective, especially for having a camera with objective movement. By removing the lens and inverting it, it is possible to get closer very close and reveal details that normally go unnoticed. With the help of an inverter, the process becomes practical, although it becomes a little instável and difficult to control. What most attracted me to this method is the relationship between the simplicity of the method and the minimally decent result I tend to have with the minimum resources, once it achieves a surprising extension and a new way of working for all types of objects, no matter how common it may seem.

https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://img.esteem.ws/qpm6pm12ej.gif

##### Used equipment & Camera Settings

For these images I used a Canon EOS 600D, a DSLR with a CMOS sensor that gives me a good response to detail and a fairly balanced reading of texture and color.
Worked with an EFS 18–55 mm objective, taking advantage of its versatility and reduced depth of field to isolate small areas of the surface and highlight very specific details. I also reviewed an inverter panel, essential in this process, for allowing the lens to be transformed into a simple and effective macro solution, as it has the opportunity to display the GIFs that part of this article.
Do not use a tripod.
The lighting was made with adjustable LED lights, designed to distribute light softly, control harsh shadows and enhance the structure of the subject.

Focus Mode: Manual focus to ensure precision in specific details of the structure.
Aperture: f/5 for adequate depth of field, ensuring all important details are in focus.
ISO: Low ISO setting (400) to minimize noise in images.
Shutter Speed: Adjust shutter speed as needed to avoid underexposure, while maintaining a value that allows you to capture sharp details.

---

To finish, i leave you with some considerations regarding these photo sessions:

> Observing all these pieces through macro photography reveals a fascinating dimension and breadth, full of minute details that ultimately assume significant importance in the visual composition. The complexity of these objects, when viewed from this perspective, takes on a beauty that is often overlooked by the indifference of the eye. The essence of macro photography lies in its ability to elevate ordinary objects to extraordinary levels, offering an intimate and captivating perspective.

The session is closed for today.
Hope you like it :)

Starting with this first shot which I took while at Fall River Heritage State park recently, I was mostly focusing on the Bridge, the ships in Battleship cove, the boardwalk and sunrise, but this reflection of the bridge in the water with the motion of the water giving it a kind of abstract feel so I took this shot. I have rotated it 180 degrees so its upside down from how I took it but i felt it looked better this way
